about.title: Who I am
paragraphs: For {years:modulesGarden} I've been building PHP backends, mostly Laravel, and working on PanelAlpha, a platform that helps service companies automate WordPress management. I'm closest to hosting control panel integrations (cPanel, Plesk, DirectAdmin), and I also contribute to the open-source PanelAlpha Engine. I've always wanted to program and build things of my own: I like technology and solving problems.

I like owning a feature from the backend layer through to working business logic — and when needed, I pick up the frontend (Vue.js). In working with others I value directness. I take responsibility for a task and see it through to the end; I work on a live product, so I care about code that actually works for customers.

After hours I build two products of my own that run in production, Domowy Skarbnik and Root Keeper, on my own VPS behind Traefik. I keep learning to work with AI: I read, test tools and take part in courses (10xDevs among them). I write code with AI agents in a process with tests and review — I'm the one accountable for what reaches production.
I live in Lublin. Outside of code — family, walks and the mountains, working outdoors, and a good book.

aiWorkflow.title: Working with AI agents
aiWorkflow.subtitle: Agents (Claude Code, Cursor) write a large share of my code, but I own what reaches production. I am refining the process in the 10xDevs course, and its traces are in my public repositories.

proof.lead: Every change leaves a documentation folder in the repository. A few that show how it works:

items.shows: Rules for working with production data (encrypted backups, a backup before every migration) set before real data reached production.
Restoring from a backup as a flow tested in CI, not a script in a drawer.
Data ownership boundaries between accounts verified by tests.
Playwright wired into the pipeline on every PR, not run by hand.
Category suggestions on import as domain logic (model, ADR, tests), not just UI.

proof.counterLabel: Archived changes across three public repositories

steps.title: Context before code
steps.body: Domain glossary, PRD and architecture decisions in a context/ folder. The agent works with the same terms I do.

steps.title: Research, plan, ship
steps.body: Each change gets its own documentation folder: usually a plan, and for larger ones also research and an implementation review. It moves to the archive once shipped.

steps.title: Rules for agents
steps.body: CLAUDE.md describes the stack, versions and what not to do. Laravel Boost gives the agent access to the app over MCP.

steps.title: Quality gates
steps.body: Lint, Larastan level 7, Pest tests and Playwright e2e in CI. A red test is a signal, not an obstacle to work around.

aiWorkflow.closing: The agent speeds up writing. Context, tests and review decide what stays.

items.title: Domowy Skarbnik
items.subtitle: A yearly household budget: plan vs actual, liquidity across accounts and term deposits, and CSV/XLSX statement import from mBank and BNP Paribas.
items.imageAlt: Domowy Skarbnik dashboard with sample data
highlights: Amounts stored as integer minor units, never floats
Architecture decision records (ADR), a domain glossary and a CHANGELOG
Pest tests run in CI on GitHub Actions
Its own design system, deployed on a VPS behind Traefik

items.title: Root Keeper
items.subtitle: A family tree where every date has a source. People, relationships and scanned records that confirm births, marriages and deaths.
items.imageAlt: Root Keeper start screen with a tree illustration where each person is backed by a record
highlights: Partial dates the way records have them: year or month only, “about”, month names and Roman numerals
Relationship rules enforced on the server: at most two parents, no cycles
Sign-in with a password or a passkey
CI workflows: lint, Larastan 7, Pest tests and Playwright e2e
items.proves: The same backend with a different frontend (React 19 + TypeScript), CI pipelines: lint, Larastan, Pest, Playwright e2e.
